rationale: Both are well structured, project-driven curricula with similar phase ordering, from-scratch emphasis, weekly rhythms and specialization tracks. B adds nice pedagogical checkpoints, a separate classical-ML phase and a must-read paper list. However, B's resource lists contain several fabricated or misattributed items. These include a Raschka 'PyTorch for Deep Learning' O'Reilly book, Karpathy 'Let's build Stable Diffusion' and a 'Deep Learning for Computer Vision' series attributed to him, 'CS295/CS341' for RL rather than CS234, the Annotated Diffusion Model credited to Harvard NLP, and DDIA as a serving resource. For a curriculum, inaccurate resources directly undermine actionability. A's resources are largely accurate (CS231n, CS224n, Karpathy Zero to Hero, Illustrated Transformer, Chip Huyen, MLOps Zoomcamp, Sutton and Barto), with one garbled author name on the MML book and a dubious GNN reference. A also covers production and MLOps in a dedicated phase and gives realistic part-time and full-time timelines. A is the more reliable curriculum.
